Good morning. Ukraine has critically damaged the Kerch bridge linking occupied Crimea with Russia in an overnight missile attack, in what Ukrainian officials say is a symbolic blow to the Kremlin. The strike follows an earlier attack on Monday that targeted an arch across its central section.
Ukraine has declared that the Kerch bridge, built eight years ago after Vladimir Putin’s 2014 annexation of Crimea, is illegal. It has repeatedly attempted to destroy it. The Kremlin-appointed governor of Crimea, Sergey Aksyonov, confirmed that the bridge, which was temporarily closed on Monday, was no longer usable. Photos suggest that a 227-metre road arch span has fallen into the Kerch strait.
Hundreds arrested at anti-Trump protests in the Philippines
Hundreds of people have been arrested in heated demonstrations against Donald Trump in Manila, as authorities braced for more protests before the US president’s arrival. Organisers say they expect as many as 10,000 people to join protests against Trump as he attends the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit.
Authorities have arrested nearly 300 people, with large parts of the Philippine capital closed off and tight security in place. Some protesters burned effigies of the US president, and demonstrators angry at the cost-of-living and energy shock caused by the Iran war tried to reach the summit at the Philippine International Convention Center, but were blocked by police.
- You can follow developments at the Apec and Asean summits with our live blog.
Third US aircraft carrier brings thousands more troops to Middle East
A third US aircraft carrier has arrived in the Middle East, US Central Command has said, making a dramatic show of military might as Donald Trump keeps his options open for next steps in the Iran war. The USS Theodore Roosevelt brings thousands of additional troops to the Middle East. Trump has oscillated between threatening additional large-scale strikes on Iran and insisting that the more than eight-month-old war “militarily is effectively over”.
The Roosevelt joins the USS George HW Bush and the USS George Washington aircraft carriers, as well as smaller navy ships, which are in the region to maintain a naval blockade of Iranian shipping.
Microsoft identifies months-old bug as a root cause of global outage
Microsoft has identified the root causes of the global outage that crippled Outlook, Exchange and a host of other software last week. An initial report identified three factors: a months-old bug, malfunctioning internal connections, and server capacity. Each of these factors may have easily been resolved on their own but, taken together, led to a major outage that was harder to mitigate, Microsoft executives said.
Cornell announces full review of Greek life after scrutiny over sexual assault case
Cornell University is to announce a “full review” of fraternities and sororities determining their future on campus, after an alleged sexual assault brought scrutiny to the system at the Ivy League school. The university’s president, Michael Kotlikoff, announced the review in an update outlining several steps the institution had taken after a woman said she was gang-raped at an on-campus fraternity’s house. Cornell had already banned fraternity parties for the rest of the academic year.
In other news …
- The US has beat Canada to win the women’s ice hockey world championship in Denmark, becoming the first US team to capture Olympic and world titles in the same calendar year.
- A judge has scheduled Lindsay Clancy’s second trial in the killings of her three young children for late March, over the objections of prosecutors.
- Dolores Huerta has been honored in a ceremony at California’s state capitol.
- Authorities investigating a bomb found at an ethanol production plant in Illinois have taken a suspect into custody, according to the mayor there.
- California is suing OpenAI, accusing the artificial intelligence company of developing its technology without safety or the public’s interest in mind.
- Several companies that received refunds for paying Donald Trump’s tariffs have put those funds towards corporate bonuses instead of reimbursing consumers, an investigation has found.
- Zohran Mamdani, New York City’s mayor, has announced he is disbanding a city police unit accused of using excessive force.
Stat of the day: Freeman Johnson, oldest survivor of Pearl Harbor attack, dies aged 106
The oldest known survivor of the Pearl Harbor attack has died aged 106. Freeman Johnson, a firefighter below the deck during the attack, told the Associated Press in May: “While all the rigamarole was going on topside, I was inside a steam drum. Couldn’t see anything, absolutely nothing”. Only 11 known Pearl Harbor survivors are still living, all of whom are centenarians.
Culture Pick: Robert Pattinson is the new James Bond – so what happens next?
Andrew Pulver writes that the wait for the new Bond is over, but that’s only the beginning – there are still small issues such as the script, title, setting, casting, branding and promotion of the next instalment of the franchise. Nadia Khomami, meanwhile, traces Pattinson’s journey from Harry Potter and Twilight to 007.
Don’t miss this: ‘His wife was horrified’ – did Edward Hopper paint his sexual problems?
In a new biography, the maestro of American melancholy is called a “sadist” and a “prize hog” by his wife – who was aghast to see their domestic and bedroom problems surface in his most famous works. Louis Shadwick explains.
… or this: ‘Nothing they said made sense’ – down the rabbit hole with sovereign citizens
Described by Mark Blacklock as “the perfect conspiracy model for consumer capitalist societies”, this is a fascinating read about how a convicted fraudster from North Dakota and a white supremacist inspired the “sovereign citizen” movement. It has blossomed around the world – wasting public resources and ruining lives along the way.
Climate check: Surge of US datacenters adds equivalent of Denmark’s annual emissions
The frantic buildout of “hyperscaler” datacenters in the US has collectively caused planet-heating emissions of about the same scale as Denmark emits in a year, research has found. Russia, Saudi Arabia and Australia, meanwhile, have been named as the biggest CO2 exporters in history in a new analysis of data since 1850.
- Follow the latest from Cop31 with Ajit Niranjan on our live blog.
Last Thing: Band of baby sea turtles swims into ocean after historic California nesting
Two months after the discovery of the first sea turtle nests ever to have been recorded on the US west coast, the eggs have hatched – and California’s first group of 75 native-born olive ridley sea turtles have been released into the Pacific. Hopefully they will thrive better than Fiona the hippo is doing at the moment – she is under veterinary care after eating a hat at Cincinnati zoo.
